# A template set built with Delims is mutated like any other.
#
# The delimiters are not recorded anywhere a caller can read: the template
# keeps them to itself. They are recovered from the definitions instead. An
# end clause has a fixed shape -- left delimiter, an optional trim marker,
# the word end, another marker, the right delimiter -- and check spans it from
# one delimiter through the other, so whatever surrounds the word is the pair.
#
# Everything downstream depends on getting this right. Reading the templates
# with the wrong delimiters yields trees holding no actions at all, and a run
# over those would find nothing to mutate.
#
# The verdicts here are the ones reference_test_template_mutations.txt reaches
# for the same template written with the default delimiters. Which delimiters
# a project chose is not something a mutation report should depend on.

muxt test-template-mutations -v --seed 1
cmp stdout want.txt

-- go.mod --
module server

go 1.24
-- templates.gohtml --
[[define "greeting"]]Hello, [[.Name]]![[if .Loud]] !!![[end]][[end]]
-- template.go --
package server

import (
	"embed"
	"html/template"
	"io"
)

//go:embed *.gohtml
var templateFiles embed.FS

var templates = template.Must(template.New("t").Delims("[[", "]]").ParseFS(templateFiles, "*.gohtml"))

type Greeting struct {
	Name string
	Loud bool
}

func Render(w io.Writer, greeting Greeting) error {
	return templates.ExecuteTemplate(w, "greeting", greeting)
}
-- render_test.go --
package server

import (
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

func TestGreeting(t *testing.T) {
	var buf strings.Builder
	if err := Render(&buf, Greeting{Name: "World"}); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if got, want := buf.String(), "Hello, World!"; got != want {
		t.Errorf("greeting = %q, want %q", got, want)
	}
}
-- want.txt --
